title: George Orwell Radio Collection
paragraphs: A radio anthology of George Orwell's novels, essays, memoirs, and related biographical dramas, including BBC treatments of major works such as Nineteen Eighty-Four and Animal Farm.
Curated BBC Radio collection combining readings, adaptations, biographical dramas, essays and factual programs about George Orwell. Frozen rows are archive objects, not one continuous series.

GRH documents the program through Legacy BBC Orwell productions (May 5, 1988 to November 16, 2009) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], Factual/biographical lead-in (2010 to September 18, 2012) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], and The Real George Orwell season (January 26, 2013 to February 23, 2013) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Joseph Millson (performer on 6 recordings), Clive Merrison (performer on 3 recordings), David Jackson Young (producer on 3 recordings), Jeremy Mortimer (director on 3 recordings), Christopher Eccleston (performer on 2 recordings), Jonathan Holloway (radio adaptor on 2 recordings), and P. G. Morgan (radio adaptor on 2 recordings and producer on 2 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include George Orwell / Eric Blair, BBC radio adaptation and preservation, totalitarianism and authoritarian power, George Orwell biography, socialism, class and political economy, and dystopian surveillance society.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including The Real George Orwell BBC Radio 4 season, George Orwell and the Spanish Civil War, and Eric Blair in colonial Burma.
